name: India Shelter Finance Corporation Ltd
title: India Shelter Finance Corporation Ltd - 544044 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Housing finance lender with AUM up 29% to Rs 11,044 crore and 30+ DPD down to 4%, but disbursement growth ~11% in Q4 and no supply-side capacity signal; growth guidance trimmed to 25-30%.

guidance.value: 25% to 30% for next 3 years; Rs 30,000 crore AUM by 2030
guidance.quote: Loan growth of 25% to 30% for next 3 years, with a clear goal of reaching Rs. 30,000 crores AUM by 2030.
Maintaining the spreads of more than 6% in the medium term.
Credit cost to remain between 40 to 50 bps.
Branch addition of around 40 to 45 for the year.
this year we will cross 20% of disbursement number which we are quite confident of

guidance.metric: Fixed-rate book funded by variable liabilities
guidance.quote: We are committed to further bring this down to about 5% in FY '27.

prior_guidance_check.quote: AUM growing at 29% year-on-year to Rs. 11,044 crores
OPEX to AUM for the quarter and year is down by 20 basis points year-on-year in line with our guidance.

summary.headline: India Shelter Q4FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to Rs 11,044 crore, PAT Rs 138 crore (+27% YoY), ROE 17.6%, Stage-3 down to 1.2%.
summary.overview: Q4FY26 showed strong YoY earnings growth, with PAT of Rs 138 crore (+27% YoY, +11% QoQ) and ROE of 17.6%. Asset quality improved, with 30+ DPD down 100 bps QoQ to 4%, gross Stage-3 at 1.2% and net Stage-3 at 0.9%. Management guided to a more cautious 25-30% AUM growth for the next three years, with disbursement growth of about 20% in FY27, citing the macro environment (LPG disruption, geopolitical stress). Management framed a Rs 30,000 crore AUM target by 2030 as achievable at 27-28% CAGR.

financial_highlights.metric: Bucket cost of funds / marginal cost of funds (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Q4 includes Rs 5 crore management overlay
Gross -29 bps QoQ; net -23 bps QoQ

segments.name: Home loans (HL)
segments.commentary: About 56-57% of AUM and of disbursements; management expects the HL/LAP split to stay in this range in FY27. HL share of disbursement rose in Q2 and Q3 to keep PBC compliant.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 43-44% of disbursements; around 98% of LAP book is backed by self-occupied residential property (SORP), per management.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Book of about Rs 450-460 crore, roughly 4% of business, mostly LAP. Not included in budget; CLM 2 adopted, CLM 1 timeline unclear.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Rajasthan is about 30% of AUM, expected to fall to 25-26% in five years. Distribution across 15 states and 307 branches.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth of 25-30% for next three years, with a goal of Rs 30,000 crore AUM by 2030; management said 27-28% CAGR gets there.
Disbursement growth of about 20% in FY27, with management expecting to move above 20% over time.
Spreads to be maintained above 6% in the medium term; marginal and bucket margins are above 6%.
Credit cost guided at 40-50 bps in the medium term.
Branch addition of 40-45 per year, reaching about 500 branches eventually; OPEX-to-AUM to fall 15-20 bps every year.
Leverage at about 3x now; target of 4-4.5x before considering next capital raise (QIP or other).
capex_capacity: Added 6 branches in Q4 and 41 in FY26, taking the network to 307 branches.
Q4FY26 disbursement crossed Rs 1,000 crore for the first time.
Digital disbursements currently about Rs 20-30 crore; were single-digit a year or so earlier.
Liquidity above Rs 600 crore and undrawn sanctions of Rs 1,400 crore; Rs 378 crore drawn from NHB in Q4 at 7.5%, with more than Rs 300 crore still available for Q1.
demand_pricing: Login-to-sanction ratio was 55-58% in normal times, fell below 50% (bottomed at 40-43%), and recently recovered to 45-47%.
Management sees the environment as cautious after LPG shortages and commercial gas disruption in some markets; no delinquency impact seen through March.
Ticket size average around Rs 10 lakh; management expects a 10-15 bps increase in ATS over the coming quarters, reaching about Rs 10.5 lakh in 2-4 quarters.
Competition: management said the market is always competitive and dominated by serious long-tenure players; did not name specific lender types.
Variable-rate book is about 15% of AUM, semi-variable (fixed 3 years then variable) about 37%, fixed about 48%.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 25-30% growth guidance versus earlier 30-35%, what disbursement growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 disbursement growth should exceed 20%, with login-to-sanction at 45-47% versus a normal 55%; growth to pick up as the environment normalises.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the margin expansion from 9.1% to 9.5% NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of borrowings fell with market rates, and Q4 NPA resolutions recovered interest not previously accrued, adding to NIM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PBC level and why is HL share lower?
qa_highlights.answer: PBC is about 64% versus 60% regulatory threshold; direct assignments and LAP-heavy book management help maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the management overlay rise in Stage-2 ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 5 crore overlay of 2% on Stage-2 assets for macro conditions; RBI minimum thresholds are 1.5% for HL and 2.5% for LAP; no plan to add further overlays currently.

qa_highlights.question: How will the gap between disbursement growth (~20%) and AUM growth (~27%) be bridged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower BT-out, which has fallen to 4.5% from about 5.3%, and said disbursement growth above 20% would add to AUM growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the prepayment composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-thirds of prepayments are balance transfer (BT) outs and one-third are own-fund prepayments; about 65-70% of the book is fixed and BT outs have declined.

risks_watch: Disbursement growth slowing to ~11% QoQ/YoY in Q4 and management guiding only 20% for FY27; watch whether the 25% threshold is reached.
Macro stress from LPG shortages, geopolitical war and uneven monsoon in rural and semi-urban markets; management says it is watching closely.
Competition from new lenders in granular markets; management says no current pressure but did not give specifics.
Rate-cut transmission: falling cost of funds, with variable-rate liabilities funding fixed-rate assets (about 7-8%) and a target of 5% by FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability, but cautious on growth: management repeatedly described the environment as 'cautionary' and said it is holding disbursement growth back on underwriting and BRE grounds, with the aim of resuming faster growth once conditions improve. Answers on the ticket-size and disbursement-to-AUM bridge were less precise.
key_quotes: Our net worth now stands at Rs. 3,198 crores.
Thankfully, our BT out is reducing year-on-year.
So, today leverage is 3x. I think we would like to go to the level of leverage around 4x and 4.5x times, basically, before thinking upon what to take a next course on that piece.
In our plan, in our budget, we are not including any of the numbers which is around the co-lending.

adds.what: Branch network: 41 branches added in FY26 to 307 total; 40-45 more branches planned in FY27, reaching about 500 eventually

growth.why: Management guides AUM growth trimmed to 25-30% for three years (Rs 30,000 crore by 2030) and disbursement growth of about 20% in FY27, backed by a 40-45 branch addition plan, 307 branches now, and login-to-sanction recovering to 45-47%, but no quantified order book or capacity beyond branches; Q4 disbursement growth was only about 11%.
